The command names the errand (buy the jar, go out to the valley of Ben-Hinnom, 19:1-2) and the oracle to proclaim there (19:3-9), then turns to the performance instruction, “Then you shall break the container in the sight of the men who go with you” (web:Jer.19.10), before its own interpretation, כָּ֣כָה אֶשְׁבֹּ֞ר אֶת הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ וְאֶת הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר יִשְׁבֹּר֙ אֶת כְּלִ֣י הַיּוֹצֵ֔ר (oshb:Jer.19.11, byte tier) — “Even so I will break this people and this city as one breaks a potter’s vessel” (web:Jer.19.11) — closing on the Topheth-house judgment through 19:13. Command, performance instruction, and interpretation stay one unit because the same errand and the same named jar carry through from the buying to the breaking to the verdict on the houses of Jerusalem; the elders of the people and of the priests, וּמִזִּקְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וּמִזִּקְנֵ֖י הַכֹּהֲנִֽים (oshb:Jer.19.1, byte tier), are named as taken along on the errand in the rendering, with no verb in the Hebrew governing that clause, and the witnesses at the breaking are instead הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים הַהֹלְכִ֖ים אוֹתָֽךְ (oshb:Jer.19.10, byte tier), the men who go with the prophet.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through Jeremiah’s public proclamation in the temple court (19:14-15) was considered: that scene still reports the same errand’s outcome, but it relocates from the valley of Ben-Hinnom to the court of Yahweh’s house and turns from the elders taken along to “all the people” (web:Jer.19.14), a scene-and-addressee shift treated here as the stronger seam.
